evidence.ref: Fixed aggregate directional feedback from the last measured candidate, tab=6: delta_primary=-0.011354706892621413
tab is an inference-time legal array exposed by RowSet, and training may use train-only labels/targets
SO.train consumes the supplied train_idx directly as Xs[train][train_idx], so deterministic index replication changes training mass

expected_observation: Predictions should differ most on users with tab-6 candidates; trusted fixed-slice feedback should improve on tab=6, and the portfolio gate should show positive marginal primary if that specialist gain outweighs any degradation elsewhere.

experiment_contract.claim: A deterministic twofold training weight for tab-6 rows creates a useful residual-targeted specialist from w001.
experiment_contract.expected_observable: Training row count passed to SO.train should rise by exactly the number of selected train tab-6 rows, prediction hashes should change, and trusted tab-6 slice ordering should move relative to the parent.
experiment_contract.falsification_condition: Reject if tab=6 fixed-slice primary does not improve or if trusted marginal portfolio primary is non-positive; invalidate if the expanded index count does not match the declared replication rule.
forbidden_shortcuts: Using validation or test labels to choose rows or weights
Applying a prediction-time constant to all tab-6 rows
Adding post-exposure feedback as an inference feature
Simultaneously retuning learning rate, epochs, negative count, or FM rank
required_components: Selection of tab-6 indices only from the provided training index set
Exactly one additional copy of each selected tab-6 training index
Sorted expanded indices passed to the existing SO.train call
Unchanged target, features, hp dictionary, checkpoint policy, and prediction function

fallback: Roll back to the unweighted parent; if the tab-6 slice improves but portfolio primary declines, record it as a specialist trade-off rather than tuning the replication factor in the same iteration.
hypothesis: Doubling the training mass of tab-6 impressions will produce a tab-6-specialized ordering that improves the selected parent's largest diagnosed residual slice and yields positive marginal contribution to the heterogeneous portfolio without materially degrading dominant tab=1 traffic.
implementation_plan: Edit only the train block. Before calling SO.train, read the legal pre-impression tab array from splits['train'].tab, select indices in the supplied train_idx whose tab equals 6, concatenate one additional copy of those indices with train_idx, sort the resulting index array, and pass that expanded index array to SO.train. Keep Xs, target construction, objective, all HP values, and prediction unchanged. This deterministic row replication gives tab-6 observations approximately double training mass in both the pairwise and censored-watch training paths without exposing evaluation labels or adding tab as a post-feedback feature.
justification: The large, repeated tab-6 deficit identifies a concrete residual segment rather than motivating an undirected scalar tune. Deterministically replicating only train tab-6 rows connects that diagnostic to the existing executable BPR/auxiliary training consumer and should shift learned item/context interactions toward this segment. Because the portfolio already contains strong but correlated generalists, a bounded specialist can succeed through complementary ordering even if its standalone average gain is modest.
observation: The supplied portfolio diagnostic reports w001's largest tab disadvantage at portfolio_diagnostics.members[w001].slice_specialization.member_disadvantages for tab=6 with delta_primary=-0.036711203406393667 over 5,170 rows and 2,212 users. The last measured candidate also had directional_feedback.tab for tab=6 equal to -0.011354706892621413 versus the incumbent, while changes on most other tabs were near zero.
research_nonuse_reason: The exact tab-6 residual diagnostics and the visible train_idx consumer directly motivate this reward reweighting. E003 only rejects increasing bpr_censored_watch aux_weight from 0.1 to 0.2 and supplies no evidence for tab-conditional weighting; this proposal leaves aux_weight unchanged.
risk: Uniform tab-6 replication may amplify noisy or distribution-shifted examples.
The extra rows may alter same-user negative pools in unintended ways.
A tab-6 gain may be outweighed by degradation on tab=1, which has 92,672 validation rows.
The diagnostic disadvantage is relative to the portfolio and may not be repairable by simple importance weighting.
